note: Geographic index. Only localities with a documented basis in the atlas appear here. Positions are approximate; the map is a working sheet, not a gazetteer. Two entries lie outside the Russian Federation and are marked accordingly. Several markers stand at a regional centre; each such entry says so.

places.name: Moscow
places.summary: Vagankovo (plague dead, 1771); the Donskoy crematorium (1927); Novodevichy, the Soviet state necropolis; the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier (1967).
entries: Vagankovo Cemetery, founded 1771 for victims of plague
Donskoy Monastery, site of the first Moscow crematorium (1927)
Novodevichy Cemetery, the elite necropolis
Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, Alexander Garden (1967)
Bersenevskaya Embankment — gravestones found used as curbs, 2019 (deputy’s photographs as reported)
Cemeteries liquidated in the 20th century, per a 2013 newspaper list: Simonov Monastery (1930), Preobrazhenskoe (1931), Lazarevskoe (1932), Dorogomilovskoe (1948), Mazilovskoe (1962)

places.name: St Petersburg
places.summary: Smolensk cemetery (the 1881 memorial-meal photograph); Piskaryovskoye Memorial Cemetery (1960); the Field of Mars flame (1957).
entries: Smolensk cemetery — memorial meal photographed in 1881
Piskaryovskoye Memorial Cemetery — blockade and front-line dead; memorial opened 9 May 1960
Field of Mars — the flame lit in 1957, from which the Piskaryovskoye flame was taken

places.name: Pushkin (Tsarskoe Selo)
places.summary: Kazan cemetery: a roofed grave-cross (*golubets*) photographed in 2013. Shown with St Petersburg on the map.
entries: Kazan cemetery — roofed cross, photograph by Messir, 2013

places.name: Novgorod
places.summary: Icons of the Last Judgment from the 1540s, recorded as coming from the Nativity monastery; the Dormition icon from the Desyatinny monastery.
entries: Fragments of a Last Judgment icon, 1540s, from the Nativity monastery (Wikimedia Commons record)
Dormition icon, 15th century, from the Desyatinny monastery

places.name: Olonets province (Karelia)
places.summary: The region in which E. V. Barsov recorded the laments published in *Prichitaniia Severnogo kraia* (1872–1886).
entries: Lament texts and performers recorded for Barsov’s three volumes

places.name: Volga region
places.summary: Provenance of the eighteenth-century Last Judgment icon (1770s–1780s) used in plate H.
entries: Last Judgment icon, tempera on wood, 180 × 137 cm

places.name: Volgograd (Stalingrad)
places.summary: Mamayev Kurgan, the memorial complex on the site of the Stalingrad fighting.
entries: Mamayev Kurgan — memorial ensemble (photograph 2021)

places.name: Rostov-on-Don
places.summary: Nizhne-Gnilovskoye cemetery: a photographed abandoned tomb, released under CC0. Used as the atlas’s single image of abandonment.
entries: Abandoned tomb at Nizhne-Gnilovskoye cemetery

places.name: Khutir Tymky
places.summary: A documented commemoration at graves, photographed in 2014. Included as a regional example and explicitly not as evidence for Russian practice.
entries: Commemoration at graves, 27 April 2014

places.name: Petrozavodsk
places.summary: Two photographed city cemeteries, Zaretskoe (2019) and Besovets (2022).
entries: Zaretskoe Cemetery — crosses in the snow, photograph, 2019
Besovets Cemetery — wooden cross, photograph, 2022

places.name: Medvezhyegorsk district (Lake Lelikozero)
places.summary: A photographed bog in Karelia, used on plate O. The marker stands at the district centre, not at the lake.
entries: Bog by Lake Lelikozero, photograph, 2014

places.name: Sredny Island, Keret Archipelago
places.summary: A photographed abandoned cemetery on a White Sea island, used on plate W. The marker is the island’s research station.
entries: Graves in an abandoned cemetery, Sredny Island, photograph, 2023

places.name: Ivanovo Oblast (turn to Reshma)
places.summary: A wooden roadside cross photographed at the turn to Reshma, used on plate P. The marker stands at the regional centre; the exact site is not placed here.
entries: Wooden cross at the turn to Reshma, photograph, 2011

places.name: Nepogodikha, Nizhny Novgorod Oblast
places.summary: An abandoned log house photographed in 2008, used on plate A. The marker stands at the regional centre; the village is not placed here.
entries: Abandoned house, Nepogodikha, photograph, 2008

places.name: Tver Oblast
places.summary: An abandoned wooden house by a country road, photographed in 2016, used on plates L and M. The site within the oblast is not stated; the marker stands at the regional centre.
entries: Abandoned wooden house by the road, photograph, 2016

places.name: Pechory (Pskov-Caves Monastery)
places.summary: A monastery built over burial caves near the Estonian border; the subject of plate R.
entries: Cave complex: seven accessible underground ‘streets’ over 200 m in all (2023 newspaper account); about ten thousand burials reported, no register named
2023 muon survey of two objects in the caves; the dimensions given are the team’s estimates
Legend of a tunnel to Izborsk — unverified folklore, 15 or 20 km depending on the source
Courtyard in front of the cave church, photograph, 2015

places.name: Mologa (flooded)
places.summary: A town at the confluence of the Mologa and the Volga, now under the Rybinsk Reservoir. Coordinates are approximate.
entries: Market square, early 20th century (photograph)
The chapel and the Church of the Ascension, 1901–1910 (photograph)
Named among the towns flooded with the reservoir in a 2026 planning article
Reported, unverified: many cemeteries of the Mologa area went under water with their villages

places.name: Cherepovets district
places.summary: Resettlement from the flood zone, as described in an article on this district. The marker stands at the city.
entries: Resettlement after the decree of 1 August 1936, with about seven hundred villages and hamlets moved out of the flood zone (article; decree not seen)

places.name: Vyatka (Kirov)
places.summary: The day of Semik given to the drowned in Vyatka, in the encyclopedia’s account. The marker stands at the city, and the province was far larger.
entries: Semik devoted to the drowned; cemetery feasts described as boisterous

places.name: Smolensk region (Khislavichi district)
places.summary: Fieldwork on funeral practice in one district, and a Semik custom reported for the province. The marker stands in the district.
entries: Khislavichi district fieldwork, 2018–2019: remembered bans on burying suicides in the common cemetery, neighbours washing the dead, unbaptised infants not ‘unclean’
Smolensk province: no washing, rinsing or work with water on Semik, so that no one in the family would drown (encyclopedia, regions named without original records)

places.name: Severny Kommunar (Sivinsky district, Perm Krai)
places.summary: Beliefs about the domovoy recorded in one village in June 2019, one village only.
entries: Domovoy beliefs recorded in Severny Kommunar, June 2019, compared with older university-archive material (Granova)

places.name: Komi-Permyak area (Perm Krai)
places.summary: Commemoration days recorded for the Komi-Permyaks, a people who are not Russian. Used on plate U only as a regional comparison. The marker stands at Kudymkar.
entries: Radonitsa, Semik, Trinity Saturday and the Saturdays before Pokrov and St. Demetrius — four recordings by one researcher (Maltsev)
A Kungur saying that those dead by unnatural death are deaf and blind except on Semik

places.name: Kostroma region
places.summary: One of two regions of fieldwork on the main cemetery commemoration. The marker stands at the regional centre.
entries: Fieldwork 2016–2017 (Chesnokova): the main commemoration falls in the Easter or the Trinity period, following regional zones

places.name: Vladimir region
places.summary: The second region of the same fieldwork. The marker stands at the regional centre.
entries: Fieldwork 2016–2017 (Chesnokova), as in Kostroma region; abstract only

places.name: Middle Volga highways
places.summary: Sections of three federal highways in Chuvashia, Tatarstan and Mordovia, surveyed for roadside memorial signs. The marker is the centre of the three republics, not a route.
entries: 299 roadside memorial signs documented 2013–2021 (Matlin); signs in Mordovia mostly on slopes, in Tatarstan in the roadside strip, in Chuvashia in or near woodland

places.name: Vitebsk region (Belarus)
places.summary: One of the three regions of the borderland material on the ‘impure’ dead. Belarusian, so not evidence for Russian practice by itself.
entries: Records on unbaptised children, suicides and sorcerers, 19th–20th century, with Pskov and Smolensk (Ovseichik)

places.name: Novosibirsk
places.summary: Cemetery demolition as reported in a 2023 interview: dated local decisions of 1920, 1929 and 1930 (the old cemetery became a garden, later a park). Interviewee’s account, no archive cited.
entries: Cemetery grove (1920), closure of the Voskresenskaya church (1929), a protest dispersed in April 1930 — all as reported by the interviewee

places.name: Barnaul
places.summary: Two large cemeteries reported destroyed in the 1930s; the interviewee calls Barnaul the most radical Siberian case, which is her comparison, not a surveyed fact.
entries: Two large cemeteries destroyed in the 1930s, graves opened for valuables, as reported

places.name: Omsk
places.summary: The historic necropolis is reported to have survived until the 1950s; fragments were gathered into a memorial square in 2005, as reported in the same interview.
entries: Necropolis recorded by a museum director before the 1950s losses; memorial square of 2005, as reported

places.name: Belozersk district (Vologda oblast)
places.summary: Funeral practice described from informants in villages of the district, including forty days of covered mirrors and an unbolted door. The marker stands at the district centre.
entries: Georgievskoye, Bekrenevo, Olkino, Klyuchi, Iskrino, Vanyutino, Pyashnitsy and a farmstead near Loyda named as informants’ villages (Razova)

places.name: Butovo firing range (Moscow region)
places.summary: Site of mass shootings of 1937–1938, counted from execution lists. Position approximate.
entries: About 20,760 names known; other pages read give slightly different totals

places.name: Tomsk
places.summary: Where the procession of portraits began on 9 May 2012, as reported by a news outlet.
entries: Six thousand people with portraits of relatives, 9 May 2012

places.name: Tobolsk
places.summary: Tobolsk consistory files on burial inside closed monastery ground (1815) and an excavated plot of two infant burials near Yarkova.
entries: Burial in a closed monastery enclosure, Abalak, 1815
Two infant burials at Yarkova, excavated 2015
